title: Remarks at Frederick, S.D
paragraphs: I am very glad to catch a glimpse of you this evening. I thank you for having come here to greet me. I have been travelling through South Dakota all day and am now coming to North Dakota, and I feel thoroughly at home.. I first struck what was then the territory of Dakota twenty-three years ago, so that I can claim to be kind of an old settler myself. I lived a number of years further west, out in the Little Missouri cow country. It has been a great pleasure to be coming through this country today and seeing the marvelous changes that have been made in the past twenty-three years, and even since I was out here three years ago. I congratulate you upon it and I congratulate the country upon it. The Dakotas have had their full share of the prosperity of the past few years, and they owe it partly to good laws, but most especially to the character of the men and women who formed the population. In the long run that is what counts-the stuff the man has in him. (Cheers and applause.)
